          ATI GUIDE

          ATI (Assessment Technologies Institute) gives the proctored Content Mastery Series exams many nursing schools require. ATI questions are written around clinical judgment: what the nurse does first, what to report and what to teach.

          What the scores mean

          Level 3Highest. Very likely to exceed NCLEX standards in this content.
          Level 2Likely to meet NCLEX standards. Many programs require at least Level 2.
          Level 1Likely to just meet the minimum. Usually means remediation.
          Below Level 1Needs a full review of the content before retesting.

          Her school sets which level is required, so check the syllabus.

          How ATI questions think

          Airway, Breathing, CirculationA threat to the ABCs wins almost every time.
          Safety and least restrictive firstProtect the client from harm using the least restrictive option that works.
          Assess before you actUnless the client is in clear danger, gather data first.
          Acute over chronic, actual over potentialNew, sudden or unstable beats long term and stable; a real problem beats a risk.
          MaslowPhysical needs before psychosocial needs.
          Unexpected beats expectedFind the finding that doesn't fit the condition or the drug.

          After the practice test: Focused Review

          ATI builds a Focused Review from the topics missed. Many schools ask for handwritten Active Learning Templates for each topic. The template types are:

          System DisorderA disease: causes, findings, labs, nursing care, meds, teaching
          MedicationDrug class, action, uses, adverse effects, interactions, nursing actions
          Nursing SkillA procedure: indications, steps, complications
          Basic ConceptA big idea such as fluid balance or infection control
          Diagnostic ProcedureA test: preparation, interpretation, nursing care after
          Therapeutic ProcedureA treatment like dialysis or a chest tube
          Growth and DevelopmentMilestones and safety by age

          Study plan with this app

          1. Take Version A in Exam modeTimed, no feedback, like the real test.
          2. Run Weak SpotsDrill only what you missed until it sticks.
          3. Do Version NCLEX in Study modeThe hardest priority questions, with rationales.
          4. Use Critical ThinkingIf you knew the content but picked wrong, practice the priority steps.
